newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset to weigh up phone tender - MD.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset to weigh up phone tender - MD.

text.p: Italian media and broadcasting group Mediaset and its partners will look closely at the terms of a competitive tender for a third mobile phone operator in Italy before deciding whether to make a bid.

"We are carrying out simulations and studies with our partners but not to enter would not be our decision alone. We await the tender with impatience because much will depend on how it is formulated," Mediaset's Managing Director Ubaldo Livolsi said in an interview with Reuters.

Mediaset is a joint shareholder with British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro in Albacom, a telecommunications company which aims to become the second largest operator in Italy after Telecom Italia.
State-owned operator Telecom Italia Mobile and Omnitel -- a venture led by Olivetti and launched in 1996 -- are currently the only two licensed mobile phone operators in Italy.
"The more time passes and the more the present competitors consolidate their position, something which risks making a third player non-competitive," said Livolsi.
The government is expected later this year to invite bids to operate a PCN network in competition with Omnitel and TIM which both run GSM systems.
"It is indispensable to understand if and at what price the concession will be given, if the frequencies will only go to the third operator or whether the other two can also use them," he said.

"If from 1998 (when the market is liberalised) TIM and Omnitel can use the frequencies, their core of GSM clients would make it difficult for anyone else to be competitive," he added. --Milan newsroom +392-66102321
